root_cause.text: In the ETS qdisc (`net/sched/sch_ets.c`), `ets_qdisc_change()` failed to remove a class from the active list when that class transitioned from DRR/quantum mode to strict mode, leaving a stale list entry that later caused a double `list_add()` when the class was switched back to DRR.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says “transforming a drr class into a strict one, the ets code isn't checking whether that class was in the active list and removing it” and explains that “if a user changes a strict class (which was in the active list) back to a drr one, that class will be added twice to the active list”; the patch fixes this by adding `list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist)` for classes moving into the strict range before `WRITE_ONCE(q->nstrict, nstrict)`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `net/sched/sch_ets.c`’s `ets_qdisc_change()`, classes moved from DRR to strict were not removed from the ETS active list (`alist`) before updating `q->nstrict`, so a class could later be re-added and end up on the list twice.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says “the ets code isn't checking whether that class was in the active list and removing it,” leading to “that class will be added twice to the active list,” and the patch fixes this by adding a loop in `ets_qdisc_change()` that checks `cl_is_active(&q->classes[i])` and calls `list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist)` before `WRITE_ONCE(q->nstrict, nstrict)`.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence and CVE/patch do support that the bug is a stale entry on the ETS active list causing a double-add, but the proposed root cause is not consistent with the actual scenario described in the commit/CVE. The patch removes active-list entries when a class changes **to strict**, and the double-add occurs when a previously strict class is changed back to DRR/quantum and gets re-added. Your wording says “classes moved from DRR to strict were not removed ... before updating q->nstrict,” which reverses the direction of the transition and misstates the causality.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove active classes that fall out of the strict range when reducing the strict class count to keep qdisc state consistent.
intent_record.what: A new loop was added in ets_qdisc_change() before updating q->nstrict. It iterates from the old strict-class count to the new nstrict value, and for each currently active class it removes that class from its active list with list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist). The existing WRITE_ONCE(q->nstrict, nstrict); and priomap memcpy remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: When the number of strict classes is reduced, any class indices that are no longer strict are now detached from the active list if they were active. This prevents stale list membership from persisting after the configuration change, keeping the scheduler's internal state consistent with the updated strict-class count.
